title: FHE head quantization gate: fixed-point encoding of the sealed ridge head vs its fp64 original
question: How much accuracy does the registered fixed-point encoding cost, per artifact, against its own fp64 original?

heads.sealed_ridge: the sealed ms full-train ridge head at penalty 1.0 (the registered serving artifact, M228 anchor 0.2421)
heads.lambda_star_ridge: the M297 ridge repair at lambda* = 30.0 (test 0.23516) — the M91 discipline: every artifact measured against its own fp32 original

registered_checks.qg1: 16-bit sealed ridge: max relative score error <= 2^-9 and argmax agreement on the held-out slice >= 0.99
registered_checks.qg2: 8-bit sealed ridge: argmax agreement >= 0.90, reported with its relative error
registered_checks.qg3: the integer-MAC path is the exact BFV arithmetic by construction; the BFV stage verifies bit-exact agreement

interpretation_registered_before_running.qg1_pass_and_qg1b_pass: 16-bit fixed point is registered as the serving quantization for both artifacts
interpretation_registered_before_running.qg1_fail_or_qg1b_fail: the 16-bit cell fails its own bound for that artifact — reported as a negative finding; the encoding must be re-registered (never silently widened)
interpretation_registered_before_running.qg2_pass: 8-bit remains registered as the optional cheaper cell
interpretation_registered_before_running.qg2_fail: 8-bit misses its bound — a negative finding; 16-bit stands as the only registered serving encoding
